summary: Summation No. 15 covers December 1946 in South Korea under USAMGIK. The dominant event was the opening of the Korean Interim Legislative Assembly on 12 December, with 45 appointed and 45 elected members, Kim Kiu Sic as chairman, a Hankook Democratic Party boycott over the annulled Seoul and Kangwon-do elections, and Syngman Rhee's departure for the United States. The Joint Korean-American Conference, set up after the autumn disorders, endorsed the rice collection programme; 62 percent of the quota was in by 31 December. Other topics include the closure of two Seoul National University colleges over student strikes, Ordinance No. 127 against rice smuggling, coal and power shortages, trade with China, the US and North Korea, fertilizer imports, price and ration violations, repatriation, typhus and smallpox, and press reaction. Many tables and charts give production, trade and price figures useful to economic historians.
highlights: On 10 December the Commanding General, USAFIK, named the 45 appointive members of the Korean Interim Legislative Assembly, including four women; the other 45 had been elected, and the Assembly convened on 12 December under chairman Kim Kiu Sic.

Hankook Democratic Party members boycotted the opening session in protest at the voiding of the Kangwon-do and Seoul elections, attending only from 23 December; the two Cheju-do People's Committee members never reported.

The Joint Korean-American Conference's second report (26 December) endorsed continuing rice collection and distribution; 2,700,203 suk, 62 percent of the quota, had been collected by 31 December, and the program was tied to distribution of 60,000 tons of imported fertilizer.

Ordinance No. 127, effective 15 December, set minimum penalties of ten years and a 100,000 yen fine for smuggling rice; 177 ships were seized for smuggling since September, and 2,266 price and ration violations were recorded since 15 July.

The College of Arts and Sciences and the College of Law of Seoul National University were closed on 24 December and students suspended over strikes, with reopening set for 3 February 1947 on strict attendance conditions.

The 1946 rice crop was put at 2,105,748 metric tons, 82 percent of the wartime average; November coal output fell to 21,667 metric tons and stockpiles to 345,515 tons, with the Hwasun mine closed by labor trouble.
Bank of Chosen notes outstanding reached 17,710,623,249.90 yen on 31 December; the first Korean cargo for the United States sailed on 25 December, valued at 112,000 dollars.

Syngman Rhee left for the United States on 2 December; Lyuh Woon Hyeung announced retirement on 4 December after failing to merge the Socialist Labor and South Korea Labor Parties, and the Socialist Labor Party expelled a dissident group on 30 December.
keywords: trade with China and United States

sections.title: Front matter
sections.summary: Library covers and title page for No. 15, December 1946, a stray rice-yield extract, table of contents, and list of 34 charts plus a map of Korea.

sections.title: Part I: General
sections.summary: Brief overview of the month: opening of the Legislative Assembly, Rhee's departure, rice quota at 62 percent, Christmas relief for 62 institutions and 99 percent completed repatriation.

sections.title: Section 1. Political Activities
sections.summary: Appointment of 45 Assembly members on 10 December, Hankook Democratic boycott, Rhee's trip to the US, the Joint Conference's rice recommendations, new ordinances, juvenile courts and 192 Constabulary officers commissioned.

sections.title: Section 2. Economic Activities
sections.summary: Rice crop 18 percent below wartime average, coal output falling, Chosen Heavy Industries transferred, notes outstanding at 17.7 billion yen, China mail resumed 10 December, 177 ships seized.

sections.title: Section 3. Social Activities
sections.summary: 4,000 Christmas boxes to 62 institutions, 2,460 refugees housed in former Japanese restaurants, dental statistics, Seoul National University college closures and Assembly coverage in press and radio.

sections.title: Part II: Political
sections.summary: Government and politics around the Legislative Assembly, then legal developments, ordinances, policing, prisons, Coast Guard and Constabulary.

sections.title: Section 1. Government and Politics
sections.summary: Full list of appointed members, opening speeches of Kim Kiu Sic, General Hodge, Military Governor and MacArthur, 1947 budget, local elections, party shifts, and the Conference's rice report.

sections.title: Legislative Assembly
sections.summary: Appointment of 45 members on 10 December, opening on 12 December, Hankook Democratic boycott and the Commanding General's address.

sections.title: Administration
sections.summary: 1947 budget to go to the Assembly, Ordinance No. 126 on elected officials (age 25, one year residence), Governmental Reorganization Board, and 97 Civil Service Academy graduates on 6 December.

sections.title: Political Affairs
sections.summary: Coalition Committee, Rhee's 2 December departure, Laboring Masses Party founded 12 December, Lyuh Woon Hyeung's retirement and Socialist Labor Party split, Popular Alliance formed 23 December.

sections.title: Joint Korean-American Conference
sections.summary: General's 26 December statement: Conference backs rice collection, 2,000,000 suk of grain to be imported, four corrective measures, and a National Economic Board review.

sections.title: U. S.-U. S. S. R. Joint Commission
sections.summary: American delegates remained available at Seoul for discussions on the basis already set by the Commanding General.

sections.title: Foreign Affairs
sections.summary: A liaison team was sent to Manchuria to plan repatriation of Koreans by ship to Inchon and Pusan.

sections.title: Section 2. Legal and Public Safety
sections.summary: Eight Americans admitted to the Korean Bar, Ordinances 119, 126 and 127, Pusan, Kwangju and Taegu juvenile courts, railway police, rice-smuggling patrols and 192 Constabulary graduates.

sections.title: Legal
sections.summary: Eight Americans including one woman admitted to the Korean Bar on 11 December; National Bar Association Central Council met 12-14 December.

sections.title: Major Legislation
sections.summary: Ordinance 119 on narcotics, Ordinance 126 on elections, and Ordinance 127 setting ten-year minimum sentences for rice smuggling.

sections.title: Public Safety
sections.summary: Minor disorders, juvenile courts, police inspections, ninth Railroad Police class of 250 graduated, prison work camps, and Fire Prevention Week from 9 December.

sections.title: Internal Security
sections.summary: Coast Guard patrols against rice smuggling and Constabulary expansion, with 192 officers commissioned on 14 December.

sections.title: Part III: Economic
sections.summary: Natural resources, industrial output charts, finance, trade, transport, communications, then rice collection, prices and violations.

sections.title: Section 1. Natural Resources
sections.summary: Rice crop 2,105,748 tons, October fish catch 28,801 tons, forestry allocation of 197,327 yen, and November coal output of 21,667 tons with mine closures.

sections.title: Agriculture
sections.summary: Rice crop at 82 percent of wartime yield, grain acreage fall, 60,000 tons of fertilizer, livestock census of 556,220 cattle and potato contest awards.

sections.title: Fisheries
sections.summary: October catch revised to 28,801 metric tons worth 263,263,249 yen; jute rope and bamboo allocations; 66 vessels leased.

sections.title: Forestry
sections.summary: September lumber output 657,740 board feet, 197,327 yen allocated on 7 December for 1,074,337 acres, and 12,420,000 cubic feet of fuelwood to be delivered.

sections.title: Mining
sections.summary: November coal 21,667 tons, stockpile 345,515 tons, Hwasun mine closed by labor trouble, Kyongju mine abandoned, plus graphite and copper output.

sections.title: Section 2. Industry
sections.summary: Raw-material shortages cut output; Standards Committee of 17 December, Chosen Heavy Industries transfer, production charts, September textile output from 107 factories, and labor and employment figures.

sections.title: Heavy Industry and Manufacturing
sections.summary: Korean Standards Committee metric program, New Korea Company breakup, iron, steel and consumer product charts, 825,640 bricks, locomotive works at Inchon and threshers.

sections.title: Textiles
sections.summary: September textiles worth 55,956,207 yen from 107 factories; cotton crop 71,981 tons; 42 silk factories at 70 percent of Japanese output; wool 8,011 kg.

sections.title: Labor
sections.summary: Labor Week activities, 6 December conference on union ordinances, no major disturbances, and September employment of 36,486 in 608 operating factories.

sections.title: Section 3. Commerce
sections.summary: Notes outstanding of 17.7 billion yen, 65 trade licenses in December, curbs on China trade, first cargo to the US, rail, power and mail problems, and North-South mail exchange.

sections.title: Finance
sections.summary: Bank of Chosen notes up 2,829,629,889 yen to 17,710,623,249.90 yen, rising gold price, and Life Insurance Association of Korea founded 24 December.

sections.title: Imports and Exports
sections.summary: 65 licenses in December against 82 in November, encouraged and prohibited lists, China trade suspended, US cargo worth 112,000 dollars, 162,462 tons of wheat imported.

sections.title: Transportation and Public Utilities
sections.summary: Railroad ties only 13 percent replaced, 34,384 railroad employees, road program 30 percent done, three customs control stations from 15 December, peak power 69,800 kW.

sections.title: Communications
sections.summary: China mail resumed 10 December, 8 December North-South mail exchange, postal insurance and savings charts, telegraph traffic with Japan up 20 percent, broadcasting equipment shipments.

sections.title: Section 4. Rationing and Price Control
sections.summary: Rice collection reached 2,700,203 suk (62 percent), distribution shortfalls, salt and paper allocations, price indexes, Pusan ration stores taken over, and 2,266 violations.

sections.title: Food
sections.summary: 2,700,203 suk of rice collected by 31 December, collection tied to fertilizer delivery, inadequate transport to cities, and imported salt, corn starch and sugar allocated.

sections.title: Other Goods
sections.summary: December salt prices, 1,000 tons of ammonium nitrate to the Agricultural Association, 9,176 drums of pitch, mulberry tree prices and 807,500 pounds of paper distributed.

sections.title: Cost of Living
sections.summary: Cost-of-living differential unchanged; charts of controlled commodity allocations and wholesale and free-market price rises.

sections.title: Controls and Violations
sections.summary: Provincial Food Service took over Pusan ration stores 15 December; 177 ships seized, 24 in December; 2,266 violations, 1,036 in Kyonggi-do and Seoul.

sections.title: Part IV: Social
sections.summary: Public health and welfare, education, culture and religion, and public information, with strong coverage of the Assembly and Seoul National University strikes.

sections.title: Section 1. Public Health and Welfare
sections.summary: Provincial welfare chiefs' conference 19-21 December, repatriation charts, 456 licensed dentists, bovine influenza, vaccine stocks, narcotics transfer, typhus and 35 smallpox cases at Kangnung, and the census.

sections.title: Public Welfare
sections.summary: Welfare chiefs met 19-21 December, 4,000 Christmas boxes distributed, and private funds raised for refugee shelters.

sections.title: Medical and Hospital Affairs
sections.summary: Repatriation chart, 2,524 Koreans arrived from Manchuria 27 December, liaison team sent 14 December, Masan sanitarium 116 of 144 beds, Sorokdo leprosarium numbers.

sections.title: Nursing Affairs
sections.summary: 28 nurses finished Pusan courses, 52 of 159 passed midwifery exams on 3 December, and 10,212 persons inoculated against typhus.

sections.title: Dental Affairs
sections.summary: 456 licensed dentists and 107 crown makers, 51,500 yen in fees for 1946, and Seoul Dental College closed 21 December for lack of fuel.

sections.title: Veterinary Affairs
sections.summary: Bovine influenza under control, with 19,727 cases and 92 deaths in Kyongsang-namdo, and 121 pullorum reactors slaughtered.

sections.title: Supply
sections.summary: 80,000 yards of cotton cloth and 8,922 dozen X-ray films to hospitals, sweet potatoes for medicinal alcohol, peptone production, and vaccine stock tables for Seoul and Pusan institutes.

sections.title: Preventive Medicine
sections.summary: Narcotics control moved to Pharmaceutical Affairs, typhus lecture tour, 26 typhus and 91 typhoid cases 1-21 December, and 35 smallpox cases at Kangnung.

sections.title: Vital Statistics
sections.summary: Vital statistics training conference 4-7 December and completion of the second national census of South Korea.

sections.title: Section 2. Education, Culture and Religion
sections.summary: Closure of two Seoul National University colleges on 24 December, winter institutes, 317,800 textbooks sold, 794 Boy Scout troops, and four Methodist missionaries returning to Ewha.

sections.title: Education
sections.summary: American Adviser's 24 December order closing the Arts and Sciences and Law colleges until 3 February 1947, winter institutes, and a gift of 1,000 books to 16 colleges.

sections.title: Culture
sections.summary: Ten ancient court books translated into Korean, Playground Committee meeting 24 December, soccer drawing over 15,000, and 16,639 Boy Scouts in 794 troops.

sections.title: Religion
sections.summary: Four Methodist women missionaries returned on 9 December to teach at Ewha Women's College.

sections.title: Section 3. Public Information
sections.summary: Rice-collection speakers, newsreels, recording of the Assembly opening, radio programs, and press comment on the Assembly, the second Seoul and Kangwon elections and inflation.

sections.title: Information Programs
sections.summary: Speakers sent to the provinces on rice collection, health warnings on smallpox and typhus, American material for information centers and mobile education units.

sections.title: Motion Pictures
sections.summary: Newsreels and photographs and recordings of the Assembly opening for the historical record, with a chart of films reviewed.

sections.title: Radio
sections.summary: Political group broadcasts, Department of Commerce talks, 25 December Military Government Hour on the Department of Justice, and Christmas choral programs.

sections.title: Press and Public Opinion
sections.summary: Papers disputed the second Seoul election, Cho So Wang declined his seat, Chung Oi Sin Po attacked the Assembly, and Chosun Ilbo urged selling Japanese plants.

sections.title: Map of Korea
sections.summary: Fold-out map of Korea, reproduced as a single page after Part IV.

sections.title: Back matter
sections.summary: Blank scanned pages and Alderman Library due-date slip stamped 1949; no report content.
